BO-1.description: Evaluate AI capabilities that combine structured and unstructured data.

BO-2.description: Find a scalable lower-cost solution for unstructured or hybrid structured/unstructured retrieval workloads.

BO-3.description: Reduce storage and indexing cost for embeddings/search workloads compared with the current Elastic-based approach.

BO-4.description: Achieve very low-latency retrieval over large document sets for downstream agent use.

BO-5.description: Validate vendor claims with real demos, benchmarks, comparisons, and hands-on proof before making decisions.

FR-1.description: Support document search over unstructured content provided by customers, including PDFs and other uploaded document types.

FR-2.description: Support use cases that combine structured and unstructured data in retrieval workflows.

FR-3.description: Support agent memory/context retrieval from conversation-derived documents.

FR-4.description: Support retrieval and re-ranking so relevant results can be surfaced to agents.

FR-5.description: Handle large-scale vector retrieval across approximately one million documents in a single index.

FR-6.description: Support a POV/demo workflow where users can upload documents during the session and ask questions against them.

FR-7.description: Demonstrate multiple chunking strategies for document processing, including fixed-length, recursive, semantic, and contextual chunking.

FR-8.description: Support isolated per-customer SaaS deployments in addition to some multi-tenant services.

FR-9.description: Support tagging or access association at the document level for context records tied to users and tenants.

AI-1.description: Provide vector search capabilities for unstructured document retrieval.

AI-2.description: Enable embeddings generation and retrieval workflows for customer documents.

AI-3.description: Support PDF/document ingestion where users may upload unpredictable document types and still expect useful retrieval outcomes.

AI-4.description: Support retrieval accuracy benchmarking using customer-provided questions/ground truth.

AI-5.description: Evaluate retrieval quality using top-k based measures up to top 20.

AI-6.description: Compare retrieval precision, recall, and latency during the evaluation.

AI-7.description: Potentially support multimodal retrieval in the future, but it is not part of the requested benchmark flow for the next demo.

AI-8.description: Support agent conversation/session data as a backend database use case.

SC-1.description: Show that document search works well on customer-like documents uploaded during the demo.

SC-2.description: Demonstrate retrieval at the right latency for the document-search use case.

SC-3.description: Provide side-by-side comparison against a baseline or current system to determine whether there is significant difference.

SC-4.description: Demonstrate raw retrieval accuracy and speed using the same documents across systems.

SC-5.description: Evaluate precision, recall, and latency metrics in the demo/POV.

SC-6.description: Assess top-k retrieval quality at top 1, 5, 10, and 20.

SC-7.description: Validate that MongoDB/Voyage offers better results than the customer’s current or simple baseline approach rather than merely matching it.

SC-8.description: Potential future success criterion: support around 400-500 concurrent requests, though this is not the immediate focus of the POV.

INT-1.description: Integrate with or replace parts of the current Elastic/Elastic Cloud based search and embeddings workflow.

INT-2.description: Coexist with Postgres, which is currently used as the application database and for some metadata.

INT-3.description: Coexist with S3, which currently stores raw documents.

INT-4.description: Fit into environments that already use OpenSearch for some customer deployments/use cases.

INT-5.description: Work within a multi-cloud environment across AWS, GCP, and/or other clouds.

INT-6.description: Potentially align with Vertex AI-based session management already in use for agents.

INT-7.description: Support content originating from connectors such as Slack, Confluence, Jira, Google Sheets, CSVs, and PDFs.

api_contract.pov_name: ThoughtSpot MongoDB Atlas + Voyage Retrieval POV
principles: Endpoints are limited to straightforward CRUD on the authoritative data model or direct wrappers around the authoritative query patterns.
No API is introduced for unsupported capabilities such as raw binary file storage, authentication/authorization subsystem management, or agent session database management beyond the modeled entities.
Tenant scope is explicit in nearly all endpoints because the data model and query patterns are tenant-scoped.

pagination.note: Only limit-based pagination is guaranteed because authoritative query patterns define limit but no skip/cursor pattern.

unsupported_or_out_of_scope.reason: The authoritative data model explicitly keeps raw binaries out of MongoDB and stores only source_uri/extracted text; no query pattern supports blob retrieval.

Rerank scores are represented in query_results results payloads, but no authoritative query pattern defines a standalone rerank operation. Reranking may occur inside retrieval services before persisting results, but not as a separate contract endpoint.

unsupported_or_out_of_scope.reason: Possible via CRUD in principle, but not required by the authoritative query patterns or POV scope; omitted to avoid inventing unneeded lifecycle APIs.
The authoritative model explicitly excludes a separate session/conversation collection.

QP-1.name: List retrieval-ready documents for a tenant demo session

QP-6.name: Agent memory retrieval for a tenant

collections.name: tenants
collections.description: Tenant/customer isolation boundary for uploaded documents, agent memory, benchmark runs, and queries. Included because Tenant is an explicit business entity and retrieval/evaluation flows are tenant-scoped.

indexing.name: uk_tenant_key
indexing.reason: Lookup tenant by external/customer key during ingest and benchmark/demo sessions.

collections.name: documents
collections.description: Top-level customer-provided content and conversation-derived memory documents used for retrieval. Stores source metadata and extracted text, while raw binary may remain external (e.g. S3) per current-state integration context.

fields.name: structured_attributes
fields.description: Flexible structured metadata used for hybrid retrieval filters, e.g. product area, connector source, labels, timestamps.

fields.name: access
fields.description: Optional access association carried at document level; included as current-state-aligned metadata, not as a separate entitlement system.

references.why: Documents belong to a tenant and are queried within tenant scope.

indexing.name: idx_documents_tenant_status_type
indexing.reason: Supports listing/filtering uploaded content in a demo session and selecting retrieval-ready documents by tenant/type.

indexing.name: idx_documents_tenant_source
indexing.reason: Supports filtering by connector/source and recent uploads during POV demos.

indexing.name: idx_documents_structured_attrs
indexing.reason: Supports hybrid structured/unstructured retrieval filters within a tenant using metadata predicates.

collections.name: chunk_profiles
collections.description: Definition of chunking strategies used in the POV/demo and benchmarking harness. Separated so the same document can be chunked multiple ways without duplicating strategy metadata on every chunk.

fields.name: parameters
fields.description: Strategy-specific settings such as chunk_size, overlap, separators, semantic thresholds.

references.why: Allows tenant-specific or global benchmark/demo configurations.

indexing.name: idx_chunk_profiles_strategy
indexing.reason: Supports selecting one or more configured chunking strategies for a demo or benchmark run.

collections.name: chunks
collections.description: Retrieval unit derived from documents. Stores chunk text, chunking strategy used, embedding vector, and ranking metadata needed for semantic retrieval and reranking experiments.

fields.name: structured_attributes
fields.description: Metadata copied/derived from document for hybrid filtering at chunk retrieval time.

fields.name: rerank_text
fields.description: Optional text optimized for reranker input, if different from chunk text.

references.why: Chunks belong to a source document.
A document may be chunked multiple ways for side-by-side evaluation.

indexing.name: idx_chunks_document_profile_order
indexing.reason: Supports reassembling or inspecting chunks for a given document and chunking strategy in order.

indexing.name: idx_chunks_tenant_profile
indexing.reason: Supports retrieval limited to a tenant and a selected chunking strategy during benchmark comparisons.

indexing.name: search_chunks_text
indexing.reason: Supports lexical and hybrid retrieval over chunk text plus metadata filters for document search and hybrid structured/unstructured use cases.

indexing.name: vector_chunks_embedding
indexing.reason: Supports semantic vector retrieval over chunk embeddings for unstructured document search and agent memory retrieval at scale.

collections.name: queries
collections.description: User questions and benchmark prompts submitted against a tenant corpus. Captures both ad hoc demo questions and benchmark questions with optional ground truth linkage.

fields.name: document_scope
fields.description: Optional constraints for on-the-fly demo queries or benchmark subsets.

references.why: Queries are evaluated in tenant context.
Benchmark queries belong to a benchmark run when part of a formal evaluation.

indexing.name: idx_queries_run_type
indexing.reason: Supports listing benchmark prompts for a run and separating benchmark from ad hoc demo questions.

indexing.name: idx_queries_tenant_created
indexing.reason: Supports recent-query history in a tenant-scoped demo session.

collections.name: benchmark_runs
collections.description: A side-by-side POV evaluation execution context for a corpus, retrieval configuration, and comparison target(s). Captures the benchmark session the customer requested, including top-k metrics and latency measurements across approaches.

fields.name: comparison_targets
fields.description: Systems being compared in the run.

embedded_documents.name: comparison_targets
embedded_documents.why: Small bounded list scoped to a single benchmark run; embedding keeps run definition self-contained.

references.why: Benchmark run may compare one or more chunking strategies.

indexing.name: idx_benchmark_runs_tenant_status
indexing.reason: Supports listing and managing benchmark sessions for a tenant.

collections.name: query_results
collections.description: Stores retrieval outputs and evaluation metrics per query per compared approach. This collection is the measurement backbone for precision/recall/top-k/latency comparisons requested in the POV.

fields.name: results
fields.description: Ordered retrieval set for the query.

fields.name: metrics
fields.description: Evaluation metrics captured for this approach/query.

embedded_documents.name: results
embedded_documents.why: Top-k result list is naturally scoped to a single query execution and bounded (top 1/5/10/20), so embedding avoids extra joins for benchmark analysis.

embedded_documents.name: metrics
embedded_documents.why: Metrics are computed per result set and always read together with it.

references.why: Results may belong to a formal benchmark run.
Each result set answers one query.
Tenant scoping for filtering and analysis.
Enables comparison across chunking strategies in the benchmark harness.

indexing.name: idx_results_run_query_approach_profile
indexing.reason: Supports side-by-side comparison of a query across systems and chunking strategies.

indexing.name: idx_results_tenant_approach_created
indexing.reason: Supports tenant-scoped analysis of recent benchmark executions by compared approach.

embedding_vs_reference_rationale.why: Chunk volume is high and retrieval operates at chunk granularity; embedding chunks inside documents would create very large document growth and inefficient vector index maintenance.

embedding_vs_reference_rationale.decision: Store embedding vector directly on chunk.
embedding_vs_reference_rationale.why: Embedding is only meaningful in context of the chunk retrieval unit and is queried together with chunk text/metadata for vector search.
Top-k result sets are small and always consumed together for benchmark inspection and scoring.
Short per-run configuration list; no independent lifecycle requiring a separate collection.

scope_notes: Raw file binaries are not modeled in MongoDB because current-state integration explicitly mentions S3/raw object storage; model stores source_uri and extracted text instead.
No separate application-session or conversation database collection is introduced because AI-8 was explicitly removed as a requirement.
Access metadata is kept optional and lightweight on documents to reflect current-state tagging context without inventing a full authorization subsystem.

Chunk profile support is included because the POV explicitly needs side-by-side demonstration of chunking options, but it is treated as benchmark/demo configuration rather than a generalized product platform requirement.
